title: The Forgotten Sigil Again
premise: Edmund Eastwick fled his hedge-witch mistress to escape the memory-tithes she demanded, but a dying courier's map drags him into the war he was hiding from: the usurper Veyra has been buying souls wholesale, and among them is the soul of Sable, the smuggler who once saved Edmund's life and whom he abandoned. Guided by the map and haunted by memories that aren't his own—the courier's, bleeding into his mind with every mile—Edmund descends into the court beneath Thornfell mountain. There he bargains with the pale court, betrays an ally to survive, and finally pays his own dearest memory of belonging as the price to steal Sable's soul back. He emerges changed and half-remembering, leading the free cities' ragged defense not as a hero, but as someone who has learned that survival means choosing what you're willing to lose.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about people who run from their pasts and find it waiting at the border, usually with paperwork.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Smuggling salt through Thornfell's passes, Edmund prides himself on being forgettable—no name given, no debts owed. A flashback shows him fleeing his mistress Maren rather than pay another memory-tithe. The beat is wary self-sufficiency, established just in time to be shattered.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Mile
chapters.summary: Edmund finds a courier dying in a ravine, throat marked with the usurper's sigil. With his last breath the man presses a wax-sealed map into Edmund's hands and whispers a name: Sable. Edmund's mind flickers with a memory of snow that isn't his. Beat: dread disguised as reluctance.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Edmund tries to sell the map in the free city of Dunmarrow and discovers everyone who touches it briefly remembers something they never lived—including the broker, who goes white and refuses payment. Veyra's agents are asking questions. Beat: the trap of curiosity tightening.

chapters.title: The Name He Buried
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, interwoven with the courier's intrusive memories. We learn Sable saved twelve-year-old Edmund from a slaver caravan, then vanished; Edmund ran from Maren partly to stop grieving him. Beat: grief resurfacing as anger at being dragged back.

chapters.title: Veyra's Tithe-Men
chapters.summary: Tithe-men raid Dunmarrow's market, extracting memories from debtors with brass needles. Edmund watches a child forget her mother's face and understands what wholesale soul-buying means. He escapes through smuggler tunnels only because the map seems to guide him. Beat: horror becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Door
chapters.summary: Out of options, Edmund returns to Maren, expecting punishment. Instead she reads the map and goes still: it charts the court beneath the mountain, where she once traded—and lost—her own sister's soul. She agrees to help, for a price named later. Beat: uneasy reconciliation.

chapters.title: Lessons in Forgetting
chapters.summary: Maren teaches Edmund how memories can be carried, hidden, and forged, using the courier's leaked recollections as practice. Edmund learns the courier was carrying the map to Sable himself—who sold his soul willingly to buy the free cities time. Beat: guilt reframed as purpose.

chapters.title: The Company of Debts
chapters.summary: Edmund recruits fellow invisible people: Ivetta, a deserter who remembers nothing of her war crimes; Brannoc, a tithe-man gone rogue; and Wren, a pickpocket who claims to hear the mountain humming. Beat: found-family forming around shared damage.

chapters.title: The Pass Called Widow's Teeth
chapters.summary: The company crosses a collapsing pass while Veyra's vanguard burns villages below. Brannoc recognizes the burning pattern—he helped design it. Ivetta nearly kills him; Edmund talks her down by admitting his own abandonment of Sable. Beat: trust forged in confession.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: They reach the mountain's sealed gate, which opens only for those owing debts. Edmund trades a cherished memory—Maren teaching him his first sigil—to gain entry. Inside: a vast pale court lit by bottled souls. Beat: awe laced with violation.

chapters.title: Bottled Light
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV among the soul-vaults. He finds shelves upon shelves of the purchased dead, each jar whispering its owner's best day. He locates Sable's jar by the sound of a laugh he'd tried to forget. Beat: tenderness breaking through numbness.

chapters.title: The Pale Bargainer
chapters.summary: The court's steward offers Edmund anything—wealth, power, Sable restored—in exchange for the map, which turns out to be the court's own stolen ledger of debts. Edmund realizes returning it would legitimize every sale. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Wren's Humming
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the mountain hums because the court itself is caged—a prisoner older than Veyra, feeding on souls to stay bound. Freeing it might destroy the usurper's power source or drown the world in old grief. The company splits over what to do. Beat: schism.

chapters.title: The Price Named Later
chapters.summary: Maren arrives unannounced, having followed her own old debts into the court. She names her price: Edmund must take her place as the court's mortal anchor so she can attempt to free her sister's soul. Beat: betrayal that is also love, badly expressed.

chapters.title: Ledger-Breaker
chapters.summary: Edmund chooses neither bargain: he steals the ledger-jar containing Sable's soul and burns pages of the debt record as distraction, dooming the negotiation. The court's wardens wake. Ivetta holds the gate; Brannoc dies buying them minutes, finally choosing a side. Beat: costly defiance.

chapters.title: Running Out of Mountain
chapters.summary: Flight through the vaults as bottled souls scream in sympathy. Wren stays behind voluntarily to keep singing the binding-hum, keeping the wardens calm—an act of belonging, freely chosen. Edmund carries Sable's jar out into daylight. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom.

chapters.title: What Veyra Wants
chapters.summary: Outside, they're captured by Veyra's army—but the usurper herself comes to parley. She reveals she buys souls to feed the bound court and keep it asleep; Edmund's theft may have doomed everyone. She offers a truce if he returns the jar. Beat: enemy revealed as jailer.

chapters.title: The Choice of Anchors
chapters.summary: Edmund realizes the truth: the court needs one willing mortal anchor, not thousands of souls. Maren prepares to bind herself; Edmund instead offers himself, arguing he owes more debts than anyone alive. Maren, weeping, performs the rite. Beat: the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: Sable, Waking
chapters.summary: Freed from the jar, Sable wakes with no memory of Edmund—except what Edmund chose to leave inside the soul when he handled it: one shared night of laughter on a mountain road. Sable knows him, partially, and chooses to stay anyway. Beat: bittersweet reunion.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Fall
chapters.summary: With the court anchored by consent rather than theft, Veyra's soul-economy collapses; her armies desert as their purchased memories return. Veyra herself walks into the mountain to face the court she imprisoned. The free cities hold. Beat: victory that feels like accounting, not glory.

chapters.title: Anchor
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV from within the court, now a place of rest rather than hunger. He tends the returned souls, including Maren's sister, and receives visitors through the gate: Sable, Ivetta, Wren's songs drifting down. He remembers everything except what he paid. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Map Unwritten
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sable's POV. A year later, Sable leads caravans through Thornfell carrying no map at all—just stories of a door that opens for the honest indebted. At the summit he leaves a single sigil Edmund once taught him, and the mountain hums back. Beat: memory as inheritance, ending on quiet hope.
